content.title: Ground Caller to Aerial Formation | Carrier Selection, Boarding and Departure
content.summary: Establish one clearly adult ground caller, a spatially separate aerial group and one terrain anchor. Let one visible signal reorganize the group's topology, select a dominant carrier through reciprocal acknowledgment, show complete descent and readable boarding contact, then close only after the mounted pair rejoins the aerial route.

quick_start.input_format: adult ground caller + distant aerial group and fixed terrain anchor + one signal that changes group topology + one dominant carrier acknowledgment + complete descent, lowered boarding posture and readable mounting contact + takeoff and formation departure
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult polar weather marshal stands beside a blue survey mast and raises one triangular signal vane, tightening scattered autonomous fabric gliders into a spiral. One white rescue glider acknowledges with two lights, descends, lowers a side rail, receives the marshal through visible hand-and-foot contact, then rejoins the formation along a restrained green aurora corridor.
required_anchors: Establish one adult ground caller, a distant aerial group and one terrain anchor before close passes.
Use one visible nonverbal signal to change the aerial topology from dispersed approach to ordered orbit or route.
Show complete descent, stable landing, lowered posture and readable mounting contact.
End after the mounted pair takes off and joins the broader aerial route.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish one clearly adult ground caller, a spatially separate aerial group and one terrain anchor. Let one visible signal reorganize the group's topology, select a dominant carrier through reciprocal acknowledgment, show complete descent and readable boarding contact, then close only after the mounted pair rejoins the aerial route.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one original clearly adult ground caller, one distant aerial group and a stable terrain anchor before any close pass. Let one visible gesture, stance or nonverbal signal change the group's topology from dispersed approach to an ordered orbit or repeated route. Select one dominant carrier for a reciprocal close acknowledgment, then show its complete descent, stable landing and lowered mount posture. Keep hand or body contact readable as the adult mounts, and end only after the pair takes off and joins the broader aerial route. The reusable mechanism is ground-to-sky ordering, group-to-leader acknowledgment, carrier selection, mounting and shared departure—not the source dragons, warrior, armor, staff, coast, choreography, faces, camera route, fantasy style, music, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish one adult ground caller, a distant aerial group and one terrain anchor before close passes.
invariants.purpose: Makes the initial vertical separation and later response measurable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Beginning in a chaotic swarm hides who is calling whom.

invariants.rule: Use one visible nonverbal signal to change the aerial topology from dispersed approach to ordered orbit or route.
invariants.purpose: Turns spectacle into a causal group response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Unchanged random flight does not prove command or coordination.

invariants.rule: Select one dominant carrier through reciprocal close acknowledgment.
invariants.purpose: Narrows group energy into a specific transport relationship.
invariants.ablation_failure: A random mount arriving without recognition feels disconnected.

invariants.rule: Show complete descent, stable landing, lowered posture and readable mounting contact.
invariants.purpose: Makes the transport transition physically usable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Teleporting onto the carrier skips the critical handoff.

invariants.rule: End after the mounted pair takes off and joins the broader aerial route.
invariants.purpose: Closes ground leadership as shared movement through the sky.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending at the mount leaves the promised departure incomplete.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source warrior, face, body, helmet, armor, cloak, staff and exact gestures
the source dragons, anatomy, scales, wings, red fissures, faces and group choreography
the source rocky coast, castle, mountains, shoreline and terrain layout
the source landing, mounting, takeoff, camera route, palette, fantasy treatment and 28-second timing
the source creator identity, Midjourney, GPT Image 2, Seedance 2, Suno and CapCut claims, watermark and branding
